reading_guide.note: Mechanical validity, semantic compatibility, execution success and scientific validation are four different questions. None of them answers any of the others, and the report never lets one stand in for another.

graph.title: Pecan embryo total-RNA extraction: evidence-constrained protocol audit
graph.notes: The model is an evidence audit, not a kinetic or yield model. Its outputs count verified claims, unresolved parameters and direct vs analogue evidence. It never reports a pecan RNA yield, RIN or degradation rate that the sources do not state.

instances.label: Pecan embryo total-RNA extraction: evidence-constrained protocol audit

models.basis: A model that publishes no validation claim through this boundary is reported as not documented. This is neither a validated model nor an unvalidated one.

declared_missing_information.reason: TRIzol volumes, incubation times, centrifugation speeds, elution volume, yield and RIN for pecan embryos are not printed in the acquired target-organism source.

assumptions.assumption: Only quote-verified claims enter the model spec.
An absent parameter is unknown, never zero and never defaulted.

limitations.source: the model's own manifest, as published through --describe-model

combined_graph.basis: Composing these models produces a system that no published source has evaluated. Validation evidence for an individual model is a statement about that model and does not transfer to the composition, so the combined graph starts from 'not established' and can only be changed by an independent evaluation.
combined_graph.execution_is_not_validation: A successful execution is evidence that the pipeline works. It is not evidence that the numbers are right, and nothing in this report upgrades a model's reproduction_status because a test passed.

target.process: E. coli 20 IBA 1 (CSH50R derivative), plasmid pIBAINS, GMS medium, 4 L in a 7.5 L Bioflo Celligen 310, batch with pH-stat glucose feeding, 30 degC

evidence: Morris, Geiger & Fine (2011), Fundamentals of Material Balances with Applications to Non-Reacting Systems, Chapter 4: conservation equations sum(inflow) - sum(outflow) [- accumulation] = 0, with no reaction term.
composition/composition/adapters/morris.py::_slot_map -- the composition-side port surface derived from a declared control volume.
composition/examples/brass_batch_chain.json -- the shipped graph that carries material between two Morris instances.

assumptions: ganjave/initial_glycerol_concentration: The upstream value must be glycerol, in this medium. A mass concentration of another substance is not a substitute, even though the quantities match exactly.
evidence: Ganjave et al. (2022), Biotechnology Reports 33:e00694, doi:10.1016/j.btre.2021.e00694. Cybernetic fed-batch culture, equations (8)-(16), parameters from the paper's Table 2 loaded as fitted.
Models/Ganjave/models/composition.py -- the model's own declaration of its ports, its required inputs and its unsupported capabilities, including component_identity.
composition/composition/adapters/ganjave_contract.py::INPUT_CONTRACT -- what Ganjave will and will not accept on an input port, in the model's own words.
unresolved: The cascade is permitted under the model's declared assumption, not validated by it: nothing in the paper seeds a second culture from the first. A run through it demonstrates that the software carries a quantity across the boundary, not that the resulting batch is the one the paper describes.

composition.note: Each instance is attributed to the paper that encodes it. No cross-model connection touches the insulin process, so a graph that runs more than one model is co-executing independently runnable models, not feeding one into another. Attribution is not composition, and composition is not validation.
